data.name: REALITY
data.detailed_description:
Our Other Games


Acerca do jogo

REALITY is a FREE short First-Person horror game, it uses a graphical style to represent the present mood of the game. It gives the player the ability to choose and get slightly different results. The game has many mysteries you might want to uncover.


The game is free with no in-game transactions. All assets are made by the developers. The play-time can last up to 15-25 minutes, depending on individuals.

FAQ:


Does This Game Contain Screamers?
  • While it is best for you to find out yourself, There is nothing that is extremely considered a "screamer".

Does this game have weapons? A survival horror game?
  • Not a survival horror game. No weapons.

Are there Saves?
  • There is no save system due to it being a fairly short game.

Epilepsy Warning?
  • Theres a extremely low chance you can get your epilepsy triggered from this. So it is fine. Though we do not take responsibility for any individual damages caused to you.

reviews.review:
"Another innocence ridden of this world." Ahem...indeed.

    I can appreciate a bit of context-free spookery as much as the next guy, but this "game" really does take that concept a bit beyond the pale. It's kinda hard to tell where pretence ends and incompetence begins, as one moment you're floating through a minimalist, heavily-pixelated forest, and the next slip-sliding around a bunch of corridors and rooms after touching some...er...black, shadowy THING in the corner of a room (or was this lack of control just an unfortunate temporary glitch?). Mere minutes after that you're being asked to run away from a monster, in spite of the fact that you can't even see where the fuck you're going. It's..."eclectic" and unpredictable, to say the least.

   Full points to the devs for creating a genuinely jarring and "nightmare-like" atmosphere, presuming that was the plan from the start and not just an eleventh-hour decision once they realised their game was plummeting deeper and deeper into the murk of incomprehensibility. I certainly do suspect an attempt to create some kind of profundity - something to do with war and terrorists and dead kids and jolly stuff like that - but if this was all meant to be an artistic expression of real-world horrors, it's a dismal failure. As a highly disorienting and sorta-kinda creepy "experiment", I guess it's a success; so given that the game is free, I'm happy to give it a thumb-up (meagre as that thumb may be).

   Try it. Maybe you'll "get" it. I sure as shit didn't. I like horror games that fuck with me, but I also like them to have those...whad'ya call 'em, er..."story" thingies. You know the things I mean. They give you a sense of purpose within a game, and make you want to play on and see what happens next. Me, I gave up on the aforementioned monster-chase sequence before I could find the two white globes which would supposedly allow me to "escape", and was happy to leave it at that. Should this game be harbouring any deep and hidden meanings, they'll just have to remain forever obscured from the malnourished mind of Yours Truly. No great revelations about the greater mysteries of life as we know it for THIS pleb.

   Honestly, as a single adult male I have quite enough wank in my life already, and don't need video games to elevate all that senseless self-abuse to the next level. This definitely wasn't "fun", but I'd be delighted if you were inclined to disagree. I'd like to think the efforts of the developers weren't completely in vain. Knock yourselves out. Recommended to masochists of every gender, colour, and creed. Oh, and the eerie sound design is actually rather good, should such a factor sway you to any significant degree.

   Verdict: 5/10.
